predictions.selection_reason: Recursive call that merges nested objects, enabling deep property assignment that could be exploited for prototype pollution.
predictions.source_summary: The 'value' parameter comes from forOwn iteration over source objects passed to mixinDeep. Source objects can be any user-provided objects that get recursively merged.
predictions.sink_summary: Property assignment to 'this[key]' (line 34) which can modify object prototypes if keys like '__proto__' or 'constructor.prototype' are used, enabling prototype pollution.
predictions.guard_summary: is-plain-object checks prevent merging non-plain objects, but do not prevent prototype pollution via special property names. No validation of property keys or protection against prototype pollution.
predictions.risk_pattern: Recursive deep merge that assigns properties directly to target objects without sanitizing property names, allowing modification of object prototypes through specially crafted property paths.
predictions.context_summary: The copy function recursively merges nested objects when both source and target properties are plain objects. This enables deep property assignment that can traverse prototype chains.
unresolved_facts: Specific usage patterns in dependent applications
Whether input validation occurs before calling mixinDeep
Presence of additional security controls in calling code

retrieval_query.mechanism_summary: prototype pollution through recursive object merge without property key validation
retrieval_query.sensitive_operation: direct property assignment to object prototype

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')
top_sast_rules.description: Attacker-controlled object keys modify Object prototype attributes.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-1321 prototype-pollution __proto__ constructor prototype object-key property-key merge assign recursive-merge
top_sast_rules.remediation: Reject prototype keys and use schema-constrained object updates.
